title.en: Present findings to a study group
title.es: Presentar hallazgos a un grupo de estudio

es: Presentar ante un grupo de estudio los hallazgos de un estudio: resumirlos con fidelidad, dar una conclusión cautelosa y responder a una objeción reconociendo sus límites sin retirar la conclusión.

teaching.en: Let me summarise the study: two hundred students kept a sleep diary for a month, and their scores were compared in a test at the end.
teaching.es: Permítanme resumir el estudio: doscientos estudiantes llevaron un diario de sueño durante un mes y sus notas se compararon en una prueba final.
teaching.explanationEs: Summarise abre la presentación: un resumen fiel da el qué y el cómo sin añadir datos ni opiniones.
segments: Let me summarise the study: two hundred students kept a sleep diary for
a month, and their scores were compared in a test at the end.
teaching.audioText: Let me summarise the study: two hundred students kept a sleep diary for a month, and their scores were compared in a test at the end.

teaching.en: The main findings suggest that students who sleep more tend to score higher, although the difference is small.
teaching.es: Los principales hallazgos sugieren que los estudiantes que duermen más suelen sacar mejores notas, aunque la diferencia es pequeña.
teaching.explanationEs: Los findings se presentan con un verbo de cautela (suggest) y su tamaño real (small): ni más ni menos.
segments: The main findings suggest that students who sleep more
tend to score higher, although the difference is small.
teaching.audioText: The main findings suggest that students who sleep more tend to score higher, although the difference is small.

teaching.en: One limitation is that the sample was small, so we should not generalise the findings to every student in the country.
teaching.es: Una limitación es que la muestra fue pequeña, así que no deberíamos generalizar los hallazgos a todos los estudiantes del país.
teaching.explanationEs: One limitation is that… admite el límite del estudio; generalise es extender un resultado más allá de la muestra.
segments: One limitation is that the sample was small, so we should
not generalise the findings to every student in the country.
teaching.audioText: One limitation is that the sample was small, so we should not generalise the findings to every student in the country.

teaching.en: That is a fair point, but sleep alone cannot account for the whole difference, and the results are still likely to be valid for this age group.
teaching.es: Es un punto razonable, pero el sueño por sí solo no explica toda la diferencia, y los resultados siguen siendo probablemente válidos para este grupo de edad.
teaching.explanationEs: Fair point reconoce la objeción; account for es explicar una causa; valid indica que el resultado se sostiene para ese grupo.
segments: That is a fair point, but sleep alone cannot account for the whole difference,
and the results are still likely to be valid for this age group.
teaching.audioText: That is a fair point, but sleep alone cannot account for the whole difference, and the results are still likely to be valid for this age group.

teaching.en: The evidence is fairly robust, since similar patterns appeared in two separate groups, but another team would need to replicate it before we can be sure.
teaching.es: La evidencia es bastante sólida, ya que aparecieron patrones parecidos en dos grupos distintos, pero otro equipo tendría que replicarla antes de que podamos estar seguros.
teaching.explanationEs: Robust describe una prueba que resiste; replicate es repetir el estudio para comprobar que el resultado se mantiene.
segments: The evidence is fairly robust, since similar patterns appeared in two separate groups,
but another team would need to replicate it before we can be sure.
teaching.audioText: The evidence is fairly robust, since similar patterns appeared in two separate groups, but another team would need to replicate it before we can be sure.

teaching.en: In reply to the objection, she conceded the weakness of the method; nevertheless, she argued that more research, not less, was the right response.
teaching.es: En respuesta a la objeción, reconoció la debilidad del método; aun así, sostuvo que la respuesta adecuada era más investigación, no menos.
teaching.explanationEs: Reply + to + objeción: responder. Nevertheless mantiene la conclusión tras ceder en el límite.
segments: In reply to the objection, she conceded the weakness of the method;
nevertheless, she argued that more research, not less, was the right response.
teaching.audioText: In reply to the objection, she conceded the weakness of the method; nevertheless, she argued that more research, not less, was the right response.

prompt.es: Elige el resumen más fiel de este estudio.

choices.text: Daily review raised every student's score by twelve percent over the month, as the diary clearly proved.
150 students kept a diary for a month, and daily reviewers scored twelve percent higher.
One hundred and fifty students reviewed their notes daily, and all of them scored twelve percent higher.

feedback.es: El resumen fiel cuenta qué hicieron y qué ocurrió sin añadir nada; los otros dos exageran (prueba, todos) o cambian quién repasó cada día.

hint.es: Busca la versión que no añade certeza ni cambia quién hizo qué.

origin.text: Study: 150 students kept a study diary for a month. Those who reviewed their notes every day scored twelve percent higher in a final test than the others.

prompt.es: Completa: «Una limitación es que no sabemos si los resultados valen en otras escuelas.»

feedback.es: One limitation is that… es la fórmula para admitir el límite de un estudio con honestidad.

hint.es: Es el sustantivo que nombra un límite o punto débil del estudio.

origin.text: The findings look promising, but the sample was small. One ___ is that we cannot be sure the results apply to other schools.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Es un punto razonable, pero los resultados parecen válidos.»

answer.text: That is a fair point but the results seem valid

feedback.es: That is a fair point reconoce la objeción y but mantiene la conclusión.

hint.es: Empieza por la fórmula que reconoce la objeción.

prompt.es: Escucha la presentación y elige por qué no se pueden generalizar los resultados.

choices.text: Because the diary was written by the researchers themselves.
Because the final test was too easy for the students.
Because all the students came from a single school.

feedback.es: La presentadora dice que todos los estudiantes venían de la misma escuela, por eso el patrón podría no repetirse en otros lugares.

origin.audio: Good morning, everyone. Let me summarise our study. One hundred and fifty students kept a study diary for a month, and those who reviewed their notes daily scored twelve percent higher in a final test. The findings suggest that daily review may help memory. One limitation is that all the students came from the same school, so the pattern may not hold elsewhere. That is why we cannot apply the results to every student.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con el movimiento que hace en la presentación.

pairs: Let me summarise what we did.
One limitation is that the sample was small.
Nevertheless, the findings are likely to be valid.

feedback.es: Let me summarise abre el resumen; one limitation admite el límite; fair point reconoce la objeción y nevertheless mantiene la conclusión con cautela.

pairs: Let me summarise what we did.
One limitation is that the sample was small.
Nevertheless, the findings are likely to be valid.

prompt.es: ¿Cómo responde la presentadora a la objeción?

choices.text: She concedes the point but argues the pattern is hard to explain away.
She concedes the point and accepts that the study proved nothing.
She rejects the point because the difference was similar in all classes.

feedback.es: Reconoce que no midieron el interés («I cannot rule that out»), pero con «That said» recuerda que el patrón se repitió en tres clases y no se explica solo por eso.

origin.text: Thank you for the question. You are right that we did not measure interest, and I cannot rule that out. That said, the difference was similar in all three classes, which makes it harder to explain by interest alone.

prompt.es: Escribe tu presentación: resume, concluye con cautela y responde.

answer.text: Good morning, everyone. Let me summarise our study. One hundred and fifty students kept a study diary for a month, and the students who reviewed their notes every day scored twelve percent higher in a final test than the others. The findings suggest that daily review may help students remember more, and this appears to hold for most subjects. Some of you may have an objection, so let me reply to one of them: a classmate asked whether these students were simply more interested in their studies to begin with. That is a fair point, and it is a limitation of the study, because we did not measure interest. To a certain extent, you may be right, and we cannot generalise our results to every student. Nevertheless, the difference was large, and it is likely to be valid for students of our age. More research is needed before we can be sure, and another team would need to replicate our findings. For now, I would suggest trying daily review for one month. Thank you for listening.
accepted: Good morning, everyone. Let me summarise our study. One hundred and fifty students kept a study diary for a month, and the students who reviewed their notes every day scored twelve percent higher in a final test than the others. The findings suggest that daily review may help students remember more, and this appears to hold for most subjects. Some of you may have an objection, so let me reply to one of them: a classmate asked whether these students were simply more interested in their studies to begin with. That is a fair point, and it is a limitation of the study, because we did not measure interest. To a certain extent, you may be right, and we cannot generalise our results to every student. Nevertheless, the difference was large, and it is likely to be valid for students of our age. More research is needed before we can be sure, and another team would need to replicate our findings. For now, I would suggest trying daily review for one month. Thank you for listening.

Hello, everyone. To summarise, 150 students wrote in a study diary every day for a month. After the month, the students who reviewed their notes daily scored twelve percent higher in the final test. The results suggest that regular review might improve memory, and it seems to work for most subjects. Someone has asked whether these students were already more interested in their studies. That is a good point, and I accept it as a limitation of the study. It could be argued that interested students simply study more. That said, the difference was large, and the findings still seem to show a clear effect, so I think the conclusion is likely to be valid, although we need more research before we are sure. Another team should replicate the study with students from different schools. For now, I would suggest that we all try daily review for one month, and then compare our scores. Thank you for your attention.

feedback.es: Una buena respuesta resume el estudio con fidelidad, da una conclusión con recursos de cautela, reconoce la objeción como razonable, admite el límite y mantiene la conclusión.

origin.text: Resume un estudio para tu grupo, da una conclusión cautelosa y responde a una objeción. Estudio: 150 estudiantes llevaron un diario de estudio durante un mes; los que repasaron cada día sacaron un 12 % más en una prueba final. Objeción de una compañera: «Puede que esos estudiantes ya estuvieran más interesados.» Escribe entre 210 y 260 palabras en inglés: un resumen fiel, una conclusión con al menos dos recursos de cautela y una respuesta que reconozca la objeción, admita el límite y mantenga la conclusión.

prompt.es: Escucha el turno de preguntas. ¿Qué actitud muestra la ponente?

choices.text: Defensive: she blames the school and will not admit the results are less certain.
Open: she admits the weakness but explains why the result still matters.
Resigned: she accepts the results are weak and sees no point in going further.

feedback.es: Admite que los resultados son menos sólidos, explica por qué no hubo grupo de control y recuerda que el patrón se repitió en tres clases: acepta el límite sin abandonar el resultado.

origin.audio: After the presentation, a student asked why the researchers had not used a control group. The speaker replied that a control group would have been the best choice, but that the school had refused to divide the classes. She conceded that the results are therefore less certain, yet she pointed out that the same pattern appeared in all three classes, and that she would welcome anyone who wants to repeat the study.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez: ¿por qué no hubo grupo de control?

choices.text: Because the researchers could not afford to run two groups.
Because the students refused to take part in the study.
Because the school did not allow the classes to be split.

feedback.es: La ponente explica que el colegio no permitió dividir las clases; no dice que faltara dinero ni que los alumnos se negaran.

origin.audio: After the presentation, a student asked why the researchers had not used a control group. The speaker replied that a control group would have been the best choice, but that the school had refused to divide the classes. She conceded that the results are therefore less certain, yet she pointed out that the same pattern appeared in all three classes, and that she would welcome anyone who wants to repeat the study.

prompt.es: Completa: «Sería un error generalizar estos resultados a estudiantes de otros lugares.»

feedback.es: Generalise the results es extender lo observado en una muestra a toda la población, algo que una sola escuela no permite.

origin.text: Because the study involved a single school, it would be a mistake to ___ its results to students elsewhere.

prompt.es: Elige la respuesta que acepta la crítica y mantiene una conclusión cautelosa.

choices.text: That is a fair point and a limitation; nevertheless, the pattern is clear enough to test elsewhere.
That is a fair point, but it is not a limitation, so the results apply to every school.
That is a fair point and a limitation; nevertheless, the results are valid and no further study is needed.

feedback.es: Reconoce el límite, mantiene la conclusión con cautela y propone comprobarla en otras escuelas; las otras opciones niegan el límite o, tras admitirlo, afirman más de lo que permiten los datos.

origin.text: After the talk, a classmate says: «Your sample came from a single school, so your results cannot be trusted.» The speaker wants to accept the criticism while keeping a cautious conclusion.

prompt.es: Escucha. ¿Qué da a entender la profesora al decir que era la reacción adecuada?

choices.text: That any study from another city is better than one from here.
That one study should be confirmed by others before it is fully trusted.
That Tom had found a serious mistake in the way the study was written.

feedback.es: La profesora aprueba que Tom pida repetir el estudio en otra ciudad: da a entender que un solo estudio no basta para creerlo del todo.

origin.audio: When the teacher asked for objections, nobody spoke for a moment. Then Tom said that the study looked fair, but that he would like to see it repeated in another city before believing it. The teacher smiled and said that this was exactly the right reaction to a single study.

prompt.es: Completa: «Otro equipo tendría que replicar el estudio antes de estar seguros.»

feedback.es: Replicate a study es repetirlo con otra muestra para comprobar que el resultado se mantiene.

origin.text: The results are promising, but another team would need to ___ the study before we can be sure of them.
